summary: Holistic UI/UX + integration panel across Med&X website + user portal + admin portal as ONE connected product

perExpert.take: Right now Med&X reads as three products wearing three skins: an editorial cream website, a dark-gold gamified app, and a hidden admin tool. The screenshots make the seams literal — the gala hero hardcodes "5 December 2026 / FROM EUR 150" (will drift the moment admin edits a price), and the portal login is a generic dark splash ("Where Medicine Meets Innovation" + Get Started / Create Account) that shares almost nothing with the marketing brand a visitor just left. To feel like ONE product, fix two spines: (1) a single source of truth for event facts so the website renders live admin data with a static fallback, and (2) a continuous identity/IA model where the website is the front door, the portal is the logged-in product, admin is invisible plumbing, and a visitor crosses from marketing -> register/apply -> logged-in app without re-skinning, re-logging-in, or seeing an onrender.com URL. Define each surface's job: website = discover + convert (public, marketing), portal = transact + belong (auth, the installed app's real value), admin = author the facts (staff-only, never user-facing). The good news: the chrome already hints at this (a "Member portal" pill lives in the website header, the PWA install prompt already exists) and the public read endpoints + CORS are already there. The work is mostly wiring, shared tokens, and a deep-link contract — not new backend.

perExpert.lane: Data integration / single source of truth
perExpert.take: Today the three surfaces are three separate truths. The portal already exposes the right read-only API (public, no-auth GETs for /api/conferences/:slug, /:confId/tickets, /schedule, /speakers, /conferences/active) and the DB schema is exactly what you need: conferences has start_date, end_date, venue_*, registration_open, early_bird_deadline, regular_deadline, and ticket_types has price_early_bird/regular/late + currency + includes_gala. So 90% of the plumbing for "admin edits → website updates" already exists. The gap is purely on the website side: it is fully static and HARDCODES everything (plexus-gala.html has EUR 150/175 and "5 December 2026" in FIVE places — hero CTA line 312, kicker line 308, countdown-sub line 317, facts list lines 346/354, plexus.html line 373 "December 4-5, 2026"). The instant admin changes a price or date, the marketing site lies. Two hard blockers must be cleared before any client fetch works: (1) CORS is currently locked to RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL + localhost (server.js line 444) — the Netlify/medx.hr origin is NOT allowlisted, so fetches from the website will be blocked today; (2) the bridges/forum events endpoints require auth, so the website CANNOT read them as-is — only the conference/ticket/schedule/speaker endpoints are genuinely public. The right architecture is a thin shared JS client ("medx-live.js") that hydrates data-bound spans on page load, with the hardcoded HTML staying in place as the offline/error fallback (progressive enhancement — never show a blank price). Cache responses in localStorage with a short TTL so cold-starting the Render free tier (which sleeps after 15 min) doesn't leave the page spinning. For the app to feel like ONE product: the website "Member portal" / "Get Started" buttons should hand off the session so a logged-in member isn't asked to log in again, and the installed PWA dashboard must lead with the member's OWN data (their next event, their tickets/QR, their applications) — which it already pulls from /api/registrations/my and /api/schedule/my. The single source of truth is unambiguous: the admin-edited Turso tables, surfaced through the existing public API, consumed identically by website and app.

Right now the app reads like a different company than the website. The site is a calm, premium editorial object (Fraunces, cream, crimson, "medicine meets the world"); the portal is a dark-navy, gold, points-and-quizzes dashboard that buries the two things a member actually opens an app for: my next event with its ticket/QR, and what I owe. To make Med&X feel like ONE product, the app's job is not "engagement" - it's a wallet + concierge for the member's relationship with Med&X. The single source of truth (admin -> ticket_types/schedule/speakers, fetched live by both site and app) is the spine that makes this credible: a price or date the admin changes shows up identically in the Gala hero countdown on the site AND on the member's ticket in the app, and the app can notify them when it moves. The website's only job toward the app is to make installing it feel like claiming something you already paid for ("Your tickets live here"), not "download our app." Strip the casino layer to quiet recognition, lead the dashboard with Next Event + Wallet + What's Pending, and the install becomes obviously worth it. Payments/registration stay frozen; everything here is read-surfaces, presentation, PWA shell, and notifications layered on top.

Med&X currently runs THREE divergent design systems, not one. The website (site_v2/styles.css) is the only one with a real, premium token vocabulary: --ink #15110f, --paper #fbf9f6, --crimson #9b1b22, Fraunces+Inter, 2px-radius crimson buttons, an uppercase "kicker/eyebrow" label system. The user portal (user-portal/frontend/index.html) uses an entirely different navy+gold palette (--bg-primary #0f172a, --accent-gold #c9a962), Inter only with NO serif, and 8/16px radii. The admin portal (admin-portal/frontend/index.html) copies the portal's navy/gold but then adds a THIRD, conflicting category-color scheme (--plexus #a78bfa purple, --accelerator #22d3ee cyan) vs the portal's (--plexus #0f172a, --accelerator #C9A962) — so the same event reads purple in admin and gold in the app. That triple-divergence, plus the missing Fraunces serif everywhere but the website, is the single biggest reason these don't feel like one product. The fix is NOT to repaint everything: it's to (1) extract the website's :root into a shared token file all three consume, (2) introduce Fraunces as the headline serif in the portal so the brand voice carries, and (3) reconcile the one canonical set of category colors. The portal already has a real light/dark theme engine (a [data-theme] system with ~505 selectors), so the heavy lifting for a light, website-matched portal theme is largely scaffolded — point it at the right tokens rather than rebuilding it. Deliberately UNDER-invest in admin chrome: it's a staff-only tool: give it the shared tokens, the crimson accent, and Fraunces on page titles so it's recognizably Med&X, but do not editorialize it (no hero serif, no cream-paper texture, no kicker rules). Admin's job is dense, fast, legible — keep it on a tinted-dark or simple-light shell and spend the polish budget on the two public-facing surfaces.

synthesis.verdict: Build it. This is ~90% wiring, not a rebuild: the portal already exposes public, CORS-needing read endpoints (tickets/schedule/speakers/conferences) and the DB already holds the single source of truth (ticket_types price_early_bird/regular/late + currency + includes_gala; conferences start_date/end_date/registration_open/early_bird_deadline). The website hardcodes all of it (gala "5 December 2026 / FROM EUR 150" in ~5 places, plexus "December 4-5 2026") and WILL drift the moment admin raises the gala to EUR 175 on 1 Sep. Make admin the sole writer, the website+app pure readers of the same endpoints via one shared client with a build-time JSON fallback, wrap (do not touch) the frozen Stripe/registration flow with intent-carrying deep links + a returnTo sign-in handoff, and reorder the app around ticket/QR + next event + what's-pending so installing is worth it. Two hard gates first: CORS does not currently allowlist the website origin (fetches will silently fail in prod while passing on localhost), and the service worker must be network-first on /api/* or installed phones pin stale prices. The biggest single risk is charge/display drift: the website must compute early-bird-vs-regular from early_bird_deadline using the SAME logic the server charges, never from prose.

integrationPlan.step: GATE 1 - Allowlist the website origin in CORS before any client fetch. Add https://medx.hr, https://www.medx.hr, and the Netlify preview domain to the portal backend cors origin array (currently only RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL + localhost). Keep it an explicit allowlist, never a wildcard, because these read routes share the server that handles Stripe/registration.
integrationPlan.why: This is the gating dependency for the entire live-data goal. Without it every client-side fetch from the static site throws CORS and silently falls back to stale hardcoded values forever. It passes on localhost (already allowlisted), so you would ship a site that looks fine in dev but never actually updates in production.

integrationPlan.step: GATE 2 - Make the portal service worker network-first (or no-cache) for /api/* data routes. The portal is a single large SPA + sw.js; if the SW caches API responses, installed phones will show stale prices/dates even after admin edits. Reserve cache for the QR/ticket so it survives offline at the venue door.
integrationPlan.why: Otherwise the very devices you most want to trust (installed app) become the most stale surface, directly defeating single-source-of-truth and creating a check-in/door risk if the QR is not separately cached.

integrationPlan.step: Write the one-page IA/job contract: WEBSITE = public discover+convert (every price/date/speaker is read-only live data, no auth); PORTAL = authed transact+belong (the installable app: register, pay, apply, check-in QR, network, profile, my-tickets); ADMIN = staff-only author-the-facts, edits flow OUTWARD to both, never user-facing. Every feature gets tested against 'which surface owns this job?'
integrationPlan.why: The screenshots show undefined boundaries (website has Apply Now = a portal job; dashboard surfaces marketing event cards = a website job). Without an explicit job map the surfaces keep reimplementing each other and keep feeling like separate products. This is the doc the data + brand workstreams align to.

integrationPlan.step: Add ONE curated, versioned public read endpoint /api/public/site returning {gala:{price_early,price_regular,currency,date_start,date_end,reg_open,early_bird_deadline}, conference:{...}, speakers:[...]} as an anti-corruption layer over the raw SELECT * rows. (Ship-today fallback: bind directly to existing /api/conferences/:slug/tickets etc., but prefer the curated route since you now have a second consumer in the app.)
integrationPlan.why: The current public GETs return raw DB rows, so binding marketing HTML directly couples it to internal column names and includes_gala logic. A curated, versioned contract lets admin/DB internals evolve without editing every HTML page, and gives one cache key to invalidate instead of four.

integrationPlan.step: Build one shared client script (medx-live.js) doing declarative hydration: wrap each existing hardcoded value in data-medx-bind attributes (gala.price.early, plexus.dates, gala.regopen), then on DOMContentLoaded fetch once, format, overwrite text nodes. Hardcoded text stays as literal fallback. Put price selection + currency formatting in this ONE place so site and app render identical numbers. Snapshot current values to a build-time fallback JSON at deploy so the page is never blank.
integrationPlan.why: Progressive enhancement: correct-on-arrival from static HTML, upgraded to live data when the API answers, never a spinner where a price should be. One script = one formatter = no chance the site and app disagree. The fallback snapshot is mandatory, not optional - a slightly-stale number beats a blank price.

integrationPlan.step: Derive early-bird-vs-regular price from today's date vs early_bird_deadline/regular_deadline using the SAME rule the server charges (now < early_bird_deadline -> early; now > regular_deadline -> late; else regular). Render 'EUR 150 through 1 Sep 2026, then EUR 175' from the price fields + the deadline field, and drive the countdown timer off the same deadline. Stop hardcoding the cutover date in prose.
integrationPlan.why: Right now the two prices, the '1 September 2026' prose, and the data-countdown timestamp are three separate hardcoded sources that drift independently if admin moves the deadline. Deriving all three from early_bird_deadline kills three drift sources at once and guarantees the displayed price equals the Stripe charge - a trust and consumer-law issue if it does not.

integrationPlan.step: Cache each public response in localStorage with stale-while-revalidate + a 4-5s fetch timeout. Paint from cache instantly, fetch in background, update on change; on any failure keep the fallback HTML silently. Bind registration_open and (if available) sold_count vs max_capacity to flip the CTA label/enabled-state to 'Registration closed / Waitlist' or 'Sold out' rather than sending people to a dead-end checkout.
integrationPlan.why: The Render free tier sleeps after ~15 min (~30s cold start); a naive fetch would hang the marketing page. Stale-while-revalidate + timeout means the site is never slower than today's pure-static version yet self-corrects within minutes of an admin edit. Binding registration_open prevents the most embarrassing drift: an open CTA after admin closed registration.

integrationPlan.step: Intent-carrying deep links from every website CTA into the portal, on the REAL domain: app.medx.hr/register?event=plexus-gala-2026&ticket=early_bird&from=website and /apply?program=accelerator. Portal reads params and drops the user on the right pre-filled step, not a generic dashboard. Define a stable slug -> route+params table reused by website, emails, and social cards. This wraps the ENTRY to the frozen flow only.
integrationPlan.why: Today a visitor clicking to attend on the gala page lands somewhere generic and re-navigates. Intent links are the single biggest 'feels like one product' lever - the marketing moment and the transaction moment become one continuous flow - and they future-proof the gala email/social campaigns already in flight to deep-link identically. No checkout code is touched.

integrationPlan.step: Extract the website :root into a shared plain-CSS token file (medx-tokens.css: --ink #15110f, --paper #fbf9f6, --crimson #9b1b22, --serif Fraunces, --sans Inter, shadows/ease) served from one canonical location and consumed by website + portal + admin. Add a per-surface alias layer mapping existing portal var names (--bg-primary etc.) onto the tokens so 500+ existing portal rules keep working without a rewrite. Reconcile category colors to ONE canonical set (delete admin's purple/cyan that contradicts the app's navy/gold for the same event).
integrationPlan.why: Three independent :root blocks with three palettes is the structural cause of the brand rupture. A shared token file makes 'one brand' enforceable and is the visual-layer parallel of single-source-of-truth - a crimson/type tweak then propagates everywhere instead of diverging again in 6 months. Plain CSS keeps Netlify serving it with no build step. Confirm the category-color mapping with Alen before deleting (badges appear in emails/QR/Sheets).

integrationPlan.step: Restyle the portal LOGIN/REGISTER and install banner first (highest-leverage seam), then retarget the portal's existing [data-theme=light] engine at the website tokens so light mode literally IS the website (paper bg, ink text, crimson actions, Fraunces on headlines only, gold demoted/dropped). Load Fraunces with font-display:swap scoped to H1-H2 + wordmark. Audit each panel in light mode before flipping the default - light has far fewer rules than dark today, so some components may break.
integrationPlan.why: The login + install screens are the literal handoff between marketing and app and are currently the most off-brand surfaces (dark navy, gold pills, different lockup). Fixing brand mark + button + background here is where the user decides these are the same product. Reusing the existing theme engine (vs from-scratch) is far cheaper; typography scoped to headlines preserves the dense-data legibility the app needs.

integrationPlan.step: Reorder the app dashboard around 'what do I need from Med&X right now?': top = NEXT EVENT (date/venue + View ticket), second = WALLET (my tickets + QR for check-in, paid/pending, receipt), third = WHAT'S PENDING (unpaid balance, incomplete registration, Accelerator decision). Demote network/news and strip the casino layer (points-to-Silver, Daily Quiz, Challenge a Friend) to quiet recognition (Member since / past-attendee / Accelerator alum badges; migrate, don't silently delete). All event facts read from the same shared endpoints so app == site == admin. Move the install prompt to AFTER first successful registration ('your ticket lives here').
integrationPlan.why: The install only earns a home-screen slot by showing what a static site structurally cannot: my ticket+QR, my next event, my application status. The current dashboard leads with gamification and buries the ticket - backwards for a membership app, and unserious for a biomedical audience. All the data is already returned by existing endpoints (/api/registrations/my, /api/schedule/my), so this is UI reordering, not new backend. Tying install to the post-pay moment gives a concrete payoff.

integrationPlan.step: Unify sign-in to feel like SSO without touching the frozen auth/payment backend. Short term (ship-now, safe): the website 'Member portal' pill and all CTAs deep-link to the single portal login with ?returnTo=<intended destination> so post-auth the user lands exactly where they were going; if a session is detectable, render the pill as the member's name/avatar straight into the app. Longer term (staged, DNS): move portal to app.medx.hr so a cookie scoped to .medx.hr gives true shared session - test the live Gala/Plexus payment links after.
integrationPlan.why: Today a member who reads the site then clicks in is treated as a stranger and re-authenticates - the seam that screams two products. returnTo is a low-risk, frozen-surface-safe first step (only the entry/return wrapper changes); the subdomain/cookie move is the real fix but is a DNS+cookie-scope change that must be staged and payment-link-verified, not bundled with everything else.

integrationPlan.step: Add a thin admin freshness/guard layer: keep admin the SOLE writer behind its own isolated login (never linked from user chrome), and on saving a price/date for an event with live registrations or a live payment link, show a plain-language confirm ('This event has a live link - changing price affects what new buyers pay') plus a 'last edited / public site currently shows X' readout. Keep it simple - colleagues edit only every few months.
integrationPlan.why: Admin holds the live Gala/Plexus payment links that must not break, and project history already flags 'don't delete a priced component an active link uses'. Sole-writer + confirm-on-active-link is what keeps the now-auto-propagating data flow from turning a casual edit into a payment incident. It must be self-explanatory or infrequent editors will click through it.

liveDataBindings: plexus-gala.html hero CTA 'FROM EUR 150' + kicker + facts list (the ~5 hardcoded spots) -> /api/public/site gala.price_early_bird + currency (fallback: /api/conferences/plexus-gala/tickets)
plexus-gala.html '5 DECEMBER 2026' date line + countdown sub -> conferences.start_date/end_date for plexus-gala

plexus-gala.html early-bird countdown timer (data-countdown=2026-09-01) AND the 'through 1 September 2026' prose AND the EUR 150->175 cutover -> ALL three derived from conferences.early_bird_deadline (one source)
plexus-gala.html 'REQUEST TO ATTEND' CTA label/enabled-state -> conferences.registration_open (+ sold_count vs max_capacity if present) -> flips to 'Registration closed / Waitlist' or 'Sold out'
index.html homepage event/date references -> same conference rows as above

all conversion CTAs (Request to attend, Apply Now, Register, Buy gala ticket) -> intent-carrying deep links app.medx.hr/register?event=<slug>&ticket=<tier>&from=website and /apply?program=accelerator (stable slug->route table)
website 'Member portal' header pill -> portal login with ?returnTo, or member name/avatar if session present
app dashboard event cards + 'add Gala' affordances -> SAME /api/public/site (or /tickets,/schedule,/speakers) endpoints the website binds, so app == site == admin
app Wallet/Next-Event card + check-in QR -> /api/registrations/my (ticket, conference name/dates/venue, ticket_qr_code) and /api/schedule/my

NOTE - NOT bindable publicly today: /api/bridges/events and /api/forum/events require auth, so Bridges/Forum dates/prices on the public website must stay static OR get a new unauthenticated read route first - do not assume all five endpoints are public
appValueMoves: Lead the dashboard with NEXT EVENT (date/venue + View ticket), then WALLET (tickets + check-in QR + paid/pending + receipt), then WHAT'S PENDING - the three things a member actually opens an app for, currently buried under gamification
Build a real Wallet/Tickets surface over the existing registration data (read-only, frozen backend): one card per event with the QR check-in code front-and-center, paid/pending status, receipt link
Make the in-app QR work fully offline (SW-cached) so the door-check use case is never blocked by a cold Render tier or no signal; Apple/Google Wallet .pkpass as a fast-follow, not a gate

Strip the casino layer (points-to-Silver banner, Daily Quiz, Challenge a Friend) to quiet earned recognition (Member since / past-attendee / Accelerator alum) - migrate earned status to badges, don't silently delete

Add four push notifications worth the permission, all derived from the single source changing: early-bird deadline approaching (EUR 150->175), date/venue change, payment/registration due, Accelerator decision. Nothing about points/streaks ever pushes; debounce so rapid admin edits don't spam

Give Accelerator a status strip (Applied / Under review / Decision) and a single Croatia/Building Bridges entry surfacing upcoming Bridges+Forum events + the member's RSVP, instead of generic marketing-style cards

Move the PWA install prompt off the cold login splash to AFTER first successful registration: 'Your ticket is ready - keep it in the app, add to Wallet, check in at the door' - frame as claiming what they already own

Re-skin the app to the website tokens (Fraunces headlines, paper/ink light theme, crimson accent) so tapping 'Member portal' on the cream site no longer lands in a dark gold world that reads as a third-party tool
decisionsForAlen: Domain architecture: commit to medx.hr (website) + app.medx.hr (portal) + a non-obvious admin host? This unlocks the true shared-cookie SSO and kills the visible onrender.com URL. If yes, stage it separately and re-test the live Gala/Plexus payment links after the move. If no, you ship returnTo-redirect SSO only (still good, just one extra login).

Installed-app default theme: light (pixel-matches the website, strongest continuity) or keep dark navy as the app default with light as the toggle? Affects how much light-mode panel auditing is needed before flipping.

Canonical category-color mapping (Plexus / Accelerator / Forum / Bridges) before deleting admin's conflicting purple/cyan - these hues also appear in existing emails, QR check-in, and Sheets exports, so staff expectations matter. Confirm the four hues.
Gold: demote to a quiet accent or drop entirely in favor of crimson? Panel leans drop/demote for brand seriousness.

Public data contract: ship-today by binding to the existing raw /api/conferences endpoints, or invest in the curated versioned /api/public/site first? (Recommend curated since the app is now a second consumer.)
Bridges/Forum on the public site: those endpoints require auth - either approve a new unauthenticated read route so their dates/prices go live too, or accept they stay hardcoded/static for now.
Gamification migration: confirm it's fine to retire points/quiz/streaks for existing users, preserving earned status as quiet badges rather than a hard delete.
risks: CORS is the silent killer: the website origin is NOT in the backend allowlist today. Ship hydration without fixing this and the site looks fine in dev (localhost is allowlisted) but quietly serves stale hardcoded values forever in prod.

Charge/display drift cuts both ways: the website must compute early-bird-vs-regular from early_bird_deadline using the SAME logic the server charges (incl. includes_gala and the 1 Sep cutoff), or the displayed price disagrees with the Stripe charge at checkout - a trust and potential consumer-law problem.

No fallback snapshot = blank/spinning price: Render free tier sleeps (~30s cold start). Without build-time JSON fallback + a 4-5s timeout + stale-while-revalidate, the first visitor after idle sees a hang or a blank where the price should be - worse than today's static number. Fallback is mandatory.
Service-worker caching can pin stale /api/* responses on installed phones, making the app the most stale surface. Must be network-first for data routes; cache only the QR/ticket for offline door use.

Frozen-surface discipline: SSO/returnTo, deep links, and re-skin must wrap ENTRY and RETURN around the existing Stripe/registration flow and touch only CSS/chrome - do not refactor the checkout DOM, /api/registrations POST, Stripe webhook, or FIRA paths, or you risk the live Gala/Plexus payments.

Coupling to raw DB columns: existing public endpoints return SELECT * rows, so binding marketing HTML directly couples it to internal column names/includes_gala logic; a rename could break the site silently. Mitigate with the curated /api/public/site contract.
Not all five listed endpoints are public: bridges/forum require auth and cannot be read by the anonymous website as-is - any single-source plan for their dates/prices needs a new public route first.
Same-apex cookie sharing requires the domain move first and correct SameSite/scope; getting it wrong either breaks the SSO feel or leaks sessions. Keep admin auth on its own isolated scope.
Light mode in the portal is far less complete than dark - flipping the default before auditing each panel risks low-contrast/broken components.

Admin guards must be plain and infrequent-user-proof: colleagues edit every few months, so an obscure invariant they don't understand gets clicked through and won't prevent the drift/payment incident it's meant to stop. Confirm category-color changes with Alen before deleting so badges in emails/QR/Sheets don't mismatch.
